correctness.rationale: Complexifying the real Hermitian domain gives the entire m²-dimensional span of z^j w^k for 0≤j,k<m, where w=x−iy; the real form is exactly the Hermitian coefficient condition. For even m the pure terms z^m,w^m cancel in x^m−(−1)^(m/2)y^m, while lower total degrees automatically fit. The pure x^m term makes the proposed vanishing polynomial nonzero as a polynomial in x,y. For odd m, degree-preserving monic reduction by p_X and p_Y leaves the unique tensor-product remainder of x,y degrees <m, which vanishes identically if it vanishes on the grid. In particular the highest homogeneous form of an element of the grid ideal has no terms with both exponents <m: any offending nonreduced term loses total degree on reduction. If its degree is n+r, n=m−1, it equals (x²+y²)^r times a form of degree n−r. Extracting exactly the middle k=m−r coefficients gives the stated binomial matrix. For even r=2q each parity block is positive definite by the symbol |1+e^{it}|^{2q}. For odd r=2q+1, k is even, and the two opposite-parity blocks are transposes of one another; one has symbol (1+e^{it})|1+e^{it}|^{2q} up to reversal, with real part positive almost everywhere. Integration against the nonzero vector's trigonometric square proves strict accretivity and invertibility. This contradicts any nonzero top form. The rank-one consequence follows by Gram equality of the coefficient vectors up to scalar phase; positive Gaussian weights do not affect injectivity. Replay: RESULT.md lines 27–69. Inspected check_cartesian.py, the saved check_output.txt, and VERIFICATION.md without rerunning uploaded code. The modular full-rank observations concern selected grids; the exact general proof does not assert even nullity m/2 or rule out pure-signal uniqueness for all even m.
